Elizabeth signed the offer letter at the co-working café in Indiranagar, slightly below the number she'd aimed for.
Instead of sulking, she opened a notebook. "What worked," she wrote. Giving a range with reasons. Mentioning the migration project. Staying calm when they said the budget was tight. "What didn't." She hadn't had numbers for her client work, only stories.
On her first day, she asked her manager, Baljeet, for twenty minutes.
"I'm happy to be here," she said. "I settled a bit under what I hoped. Could we set a pay review for nine months from now, and agree what results would make a strong case?"
Baljeet thought about it. "Nine months works. If you get the onboarding time for new clients down, and lead one launch, we'll talk."
Elizabeth wrote the date on the first page of the notebook and drew a box around it.

qa.q: Where did Elizabeth sign the offer letter?
qa.a: At the co-working café in Indiranagar.

qa.q: How did Elizabeth feel about settling slightly below her target?
qa.a: She felt a little disappointed but stayed determined, choosing to learn from it instead of sulking.

qa.q: What else could Elizabeth do over the nine months to strengthen the next request?
qa.a: She could keep a monthly record of results, such as the onboarding time and the launch, so she has numbers rather than stories next time.

qa.q: How might Baljeet see Elizabeth's request on her first day?
qa.a: Baljeet may be impressed that she asked for clear targets early, which makes the future review fairer and easier to judge.

"So? Did you get it?" Deepika asked, handing Kashish a plate of pakoras.
"I got the job. Not quite the number I wanted."
"How far off?"
"A little. Not a disaster."
"Are you annoyed?"
"For about an hour I was. Then I made a list." Kashish pulled out her phone. "What worked: I had my market research, I stayed calm. What didn't: I couldn't show numbers from my last project, only that it went well."
"And now?"
"Now I've asked my new manager for a review date. October. We agreed on two things: I cut the report turnaround time, and I take over the vendor dashboard."
"And then you ask again?"
"Then I ask again. With proof this time."
Deepika grinned. "Look at you, planning your raise before your first day."
"Somebody has to," Kashish laughed.

qa.q: Which other approach could suit Kashish if the new manager later tried to delay the October review?
